decisions.executionNote: Begin left support approach with elbow-up continuity; object position estimated from head RGB. Right arm remains parked.
Align and close around inner left white support, with a shallow downward approach. Retention will be checked visually.
Lift left support and translate toward its base position, keeping grip closed; begin right support approach independently without crossing.
Set left base support onto table and release; refine right grasp from wrist view by moving rearward and down with jaws open.
Close right fingers after small wrist-image alignment and lift to verify retention. Retract left clear of the released base support.
Carry visually retained right support above its base location. Rotate empty left gripper toward the long-board end grasp while staying in left workspace.
Gently seat and release right base support. Finish orienting and lowering empty left gripper toward the long board's left end; verify alignment before closing.
Clear the released right support vertically, then move outward and rotate for the right board-end grasp. Left waits open at the opposite end.
Replan from interrupted pose with smaller right-arm rotation and translation increments, finishing the board-end orientation above the table.
Lower right gripper to match the left board-end grasp, then close both around the long board. Check retention before translating to supports.
Lift the long board level with both grippers closed, then carry it toward the two upright base supports without changing its orientation.
Center the long board over both base supports, lower it gently, open both grippers, and retreat outward/upward to inspect stability.
Lower board appears stable after release. Reorient both empty grippers above their remaining white supports, maintaining clearance from the completed base layer.
Finish the block-grasp orientations and descend with open fingers. Pause for wrist-image alignment before closing on the two middle supports.
Use wrist RGB to center each remaining support between the fingers, close, then lift vertically to verify retention before moving toward the lower board.
Both supports appear retained. Raise them clear of the lower board and transport inward above the middle-layer support positions, keeping both upright.
Place the two retained supports symmetrically on the stable lower board, lower slowly for contact, and release without tilting them.
Withdraw open grippers above the newly placed supports, then move toward the shorter board while beginning mirrored end-grasp orientations.
Complete mirrored board-end orientations while descending above the shorter board; keep fingers open and preserve elbow-up continuity.
Descend to the shorter board's end-grasp height, close both grippers, and make a small level test lift to inspect retention.
Lift the retained shorter board level above the middle supports, then start carrying it rearward toward the tower with both grippers closed.
Carry the middle board centered over the upright supports, then lower level to their tops; keep both grips closed until placement is inspected.
Release the centered middle board and retreat clear of it. Move the left arm toward the small wooden top board while the right arm starts withdrawing.
Approach the small wooden board with the left gripper turned forward and open; continue retracting the empty right arm toward home. Middle layer remains visibly centered.
Lower the left gripper to the small board and correct its lateral alignment using RGB. Finish bringing the empty right arm home, then inspect before grasping.
Correct the small board's wrist-image lateral offset, close the left gripper at table level, and make a small test lift; right arm holds at home.
The small board is visibly retained. Raise it clear of the tower, then begin a level world-yaw turn and inward transfer with the left arm only.
Finish rotating the retained small board horizontally and carry it above the tower center. Keep height until the final alignment can be checked.
Align the small board at tower center, lower gently onto the middle board, and release while holding the left wrist steady.
Withdraw the left gripper clear of the released top board and start returning it home. Begin a conservative elbow-up right-arm approach to the green top piece.
The middle board shifted off its supports during withdrawal. Pause the green-piece plan and approach the displaced board's two ends to recover it, with the small board still resting on it.
Complete the recovery end-grasp alignment and descend cautiously above the fallen middle board. Keep fingers open and inspect clearance from the lower layer before grasping.
Left descent met an obstruction near the support, so withdraw it up and forward. Use the unobstructed right end to grip and gently draw the fallen board forward for a safer two-arm recovery.
Right fingers did not retain the board. Reopen and correct the fore-aft alignment from the visible board edges before another right-end grasp; keep left clear.
Make a slow right-only test lift from the recovery grasp, then a short forward separation. Retention and any interference with the lower layer remain uncertain.
The board stayed on the table during the test lift. Reopen and move the right grasp inward and lower at the forward end, away from the lower layer, then close for another retention check.
Test retention at the corrected right-end grasp by lifting slowly and drawing the board clear of the base supports. Keep left stationary and monitor the small board on top.
Right grip now visibly retains the recovered board. Bring the open left gripper down to its opposite end and close to support a level two-arm replacement, without releasing the right.
Refine the left end grasp using its wrist view: reopen, slightly lower and shift rearward, then close. Make a short coordinated lift to check that both ends are supported.
Both ends now appear engaged. Lift the recovered board and its small board together clear of the supports, then gently correct yaw while translating rearward toward the tower.
Level the recovered board by raising its left end and lowering its right slightly, then center it over the supports and descend cautiously. Keep both grippers closed until seating is confirmed.

Seat and release the recovered middle board, then withdraw both open grippers horizontally outward before lifting, to avoid catching the board from underneath. Inspect the displaced small top board next.
Clear both open grippers farther outward and upward, then pause to inspect the recovered middle layer and locate the small board that slid behind it.
Move the right wrist above the rear of the tower to view the displaced small board before descending. Retract and reorient the empty left arm toward home without disturbing the layers.

Replan after the continuity rejection by lowering the right arm first, then moving inward toward the small board visible behind the tower. Keep clear of the supported layers; continue left-arm return.
Right fingers appear to contact the back edge of the tower. Narrow the opening before a small, slow descent toward the small board, monitoring obstruction; finish left-arm return to origin.

Stop the obstructed descent and clear the tower outward/upward. Move behind it and orient the right gripper more vertically for a safer small-board pickup; the middle board will require replacement again.

After the IK interruption, reduce reach by lowering while gradually turning the right gripper toward a vertical approach behind the tower. Use small continuous increments and inspect the small-board alignment.
The rear approach reached an IK limit. Reverse the recent accepted approach in small increments, then clear the right side of the tower before attempting recovery from the accessible front.
Return the right arm to the accessible front, clear of the tower, and bring the left arm forward for a two-end recovery. Inspect the lower layer before replacing the middle board.
Inspect and align above the long board's ends with both grippers open. Its apparent tilt and the shifted supports make a blind middle-board replacement unsafe.
The long board appears tilted on edge. Attempt a careful two-end grasp and small test lift, keeping the base supports undisturbed before correcting the board's orientation.
The long board did not follow the test lift, so reopen and lower both end grasps to the board's actual height. Close without translating it, then inspect engagement before any orientation correction.

The long board now appears flatter between the fingers. Lift it slightly, shift forward to center it over the two base supports, then seat and release it before reassessing the displaced upper supports.
Fully disengage both open grippers by moving outward before lifting. Inspect the long board without finger contact; its edge-on appearance makes its orientation uncertain.
Wrist views suggest the long board lies behind the previous grasps. Re-align both open grippers rearward and inward above its ends, keeping clearance until the actual board position is clearer.
Use the now-centered wrist views to refine the long-board end grasps, especially the farther right end. Close both and make a short test lift without horizontal movement.
The closed fingers did not retain the long board. Reopen and descend in small increments to its lower actual contact height, with a modest inward correction on the left; inspect before lifting again.
Hold both newly closed grasps and make a slow vertical test lift only. Confirm that the long board follows both hands before trying to flatten or reposition it.

The long board now visibly follows both grippers but is standing on its edge. Begin a slow coordinated roll toward horizontal, moving both wrists around the grasp line to keep the board clear of its supports.
Continue the controlled roll toward a horizontal board while shifting its center forward above the two base supports. Keep both grasps closed and postpone release until the board is level.
Finish leveling the long board, lower a short distance over its base supports, and release. Withdraw horizontally outward before lifting so the fingers do not drag the board.
The lower board is now horizontal and released. Lift both empty grippers clear and begin reorienting for the displaced upper supports, avoiding any contact with the restored lower layer.
The long board's resting orientation remains uncertain and appears too far rearward. Reorient the open grippers above its ends for a more forward-centered replacement before adding upper pieces.
Finish the mirrored end-grasp orientations and descend to the board, keeping fingers open until aligned. Close both to prepare a forward translation away from the rear pieces.
Lift both board ends clear, then carry the board forward over the base-support centers without changing its current orientation. Inspect the retained board before lowering.

The retained board remains on edge. Raise it clear of the base blocks, then begin another controlled leveling roll using a larger wrist arc to better preserve its observed center and avoid pushing the supports.
Continue the coordinated leveling roll with closed grippers, preserving clearance and making a small rearward centering correction. Inspect the board over the base supports before releasing.

Stop the rejected roll rather than folding the elbows downward. With the board now nearly horizontal over the blocks, make a small clearance and centering adjustment, release, and withdraw outward to let it settle.
The released lower board is resting across the base blocks. Raise and reorient both empty grippers clear of it, then approach the two displaced white supports from above without crossing arms.
The lower board slid forward after release and is now flat. Reorient both empty hands for a flat two-end grasp above its current location, rather than adding blocks to an unstable base.
Correct both grasps forward using the wrist-image offsets, then descend to the flat board's actual height and close. Do not move the board horizontally until retention is checked.
